Knife attacks in Table Mountain Reserve

By: Annalise Lubbe | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Horror attacks in the Table Mountain Reserve has spread fear amongst hikers. Tonight we bring you the story of a group of 9 hikers who were mugged at knifepoint in the Silvermine area.

Unique Selling Point:
We track the story of a horrific attack on 9 hikers in the Silvermine area of Table Mountain Reserve when a peaceful walk turns into a nightmare. This is just one of many recent attacks that have the community and visitors up in arms. Why is this happening and what is SANPark who are the custodians of the park doing about the drastic escalation of crime stats in the Reserve.



Summary:
It was a Saturday morning when forty-nine-year Michael Traut from Retreat in Cape Town joined a small group of hikers on the Silvermine trail. The group was led by an experienced hiker Anwar Adams who gave a brief tooltalk before they set out on a comfortable pace. The group consisted of mostly elderly people, amongst them a British couple, Dan and Yvonne Cormack. It was a perfect sunny day with little wind and breathtaking scenes along the path to make this the perfect hike. Michael made small-talk with Dan and took a memorable picture on route. Little did he know that their fate was about to change.

Two men appeared from behind a bush. They were flicking their knives and shouted at the group to hand over their phones, cameras and rucksacks. Dan put up a fight and got stabbed multiple times as he tried to resist. His wife Yvonne picked up a stick and hit the attacker shouting “leave my husband alone”. The attacker retaliated and stabbed Yvonne in the arm. Michael was next. A rock struck his jawbone and he was stabbed in the hand. Michael threw down his phone, camera and wallet then fell on the ground in a dizzy spell. Anwar ran to a high point for cellphone signal and to call for help. The second attacker ran after Anwar and and stopped him in his tracks with a blow on the head. Anwar fell down. The attackers fled from the scene with their loot.



Further information:
On the same route that morning a group of young hikers saw blood spots on the rocks and started following the tracks. It led them to a secluded area high up in the mountain where they found Anwar and his group of hikers badly injured and in desperate need of medical attention. They put a call through to Cape Metro Rescue Services describing the situation and type of injuries. A helicopter, ambulance services and 4x4 rescue vehicles were dispatched. On the rescue operation was Andre Yon from Cape Medical Response (CMR) who were instrumental in the rescue mission and getting the patients to hospital.

Anwar was in ICU for several days. His memory failed him to the exact events but his spirit is alive. When I visited him in hospital a few days ago he said: “More must be done. I want to get back so I can do something about this - be part of a solution.” Michael is back at his home in Retreat supported by his loving wife and daughter. He suffers from severe headaches, struggles to speak as he lost several teeth and injured his jawbone. “Bring back the death penalty, he says.” Yvonne told me that she will not allow this traumatic incident to keep her away from what she love most, and that is to walk in the mountains with her husband Don. He is still heavily traumatised by the event that changed their holiday into a nightmare.
The attack on Anwar’s group was not an isolated incident. On that same morning 2 more knife attacks on hikers were reported in the Table Mountain Reserve.

SANParks who were informed of the attacks said “Management would like to caution the public not to take the law in their own hands and not to interfere in any official law enforcement duties.” An ironic statement by Merle Collins, Regional Communications Manager of SANParks as their role is to monitor the Reserve and keep it safe. SANParks were nowhere to be seen on that day in the vicinity of the hikers, or on any other day, as many victims will repeat the same sentiment about their blatant absence in the Reserve on any given day.

The horror scene described above is just one more on a list of growing statistics of armed attacks in the Table Mountain Reserve. Andre van Schalkwyk from a social network group, Table Mountain Watch have built up a database of stats that show pre-2000 crime in the Park was remarkably low; it peaked in 2004; increased in 2008 and rose dramatically in 2011 and beyond. Van Schalkwyk has tried to set up a Safety Forum network to meet monthly with the Park, City Metro Police, Law Enforcement, SAPS, Table Mountain Park Safety rangers and even Metro Traffic to access sensitive areas or hot spots where crime is prevalent. But this has amounted to nought as SANParks claim “we will look after our own safety’.

But crime speaks volumes. SANParks is clearly not capable of performing their task successfully and for this reason private security companies have been contracted to protect communities. All along the south Peninsula neighbourhood watch have been instituted to fight crime. However security guards have been told in no uncertain terms to “get off SANParks ground” when they try and protect citizens. Joseph Padbury of Komwatch (Kommetjie Neighbourhood Watch) recalls an incident where two people were attacked on Noordhoek beach hours after SANParks patrol unit told them to get off the beach. (Noordhoek Beach and Sandy Bay are the only two beaches in Cape Town that falls under SANParks protection and is therefor their responsibility to keep these areas safe.)

According to SANParks they have 52 dedicated trained staff equipped with dogs, vehicles and radios to monitor and patrol the 221 sq km Park. They take the view that “it is a vast open area” but do not welcome any assistance from the outside.

Frank Dwyer, a registered mountain tour-guide for 30 years here in the Cape has seen the numbers drop as crime escalates. Some overnight hiking camps have been abandoned and closed for ‘safety reasons’. He is saddened by the lack of concern from the Parks to keep this national heritage site a ‘must see attraction’ for both local and international tourists.

We add to our story the latest stabbing on a hiker two weeks after the stabbing on the 9 hiker took place. Julia and Douglas Nolten were hiking in the same are when Douglas was stabbed multiple times and eventually bled to death.
Our story:
We will hear from the victims who were held at knifepoint and share their horrific story of what they experienced on that Saturday morning hike.
We will put SANParks on the spot on why they have not been visible enough to protect hikers from incidents like these and there lack of cooperation with other organisations to ‘work together’ in fighting crime.
Through this programme I hope to bring a sense of urgency to taking action by all the relevant parties in bringing down the crime statistics and making the Table Mountain Reserve a safe place for everyone to enjoy again.

Press Release:


Table Mountain Knife Attacks
Last week yet another hiker was robbed, stabbed and killed in the Table Mountain reserve, while recently a group of 9 hikers were mugged at knifepoint. Regular visitors are up in arms, saying their security and that of tourists should be ensured. Carte Blanche asks: why has very little been done about the safety of visitors at one of Cape Town’s prime tourist attractions?


Script:


FINAL: 2 FEBRUARY 2018
SCRIPT AND PROMOS: Knife attacks in Table Mountain National Park
Duration: 8 minutes
Producer: Annalise Lubbe

V/O In a spate of knife attacks on hikers in the Table Mountain Reserve, there have been many severe injuries. The last attack on a hiker cost him his life.

Music up

V/O 57 year old Douglas Nolten lived here in St. James with his wife Julia, and three grown-up children. One week ago he was still alive. Doug is the latest victim of knife attacks in the Table Mountain National Park. Doug was a pilot and married to Julia for 27 years.

Julia Nolten: And for the first time ever I had a pepper spray with me which I never do and Douglas had a stick.

V/O On Sunday the 28th of January, Doug and Julia set out on their hike in the Echo valley above St. James in Cape Town. They were apprehensive as they had heard about an attack on 9 hikers two weeks earlier. They walked in single file when Julia became aware of someone behind Doug.

Julia Nolten: At that moment I just knew that something would happen and then he pulled out a very very big knife. He took the knife and hammered it into his shoulders and neck and that is when I just turned around and ran away.

V/O Julia managed to find help but by the time a paramedic from CMR got to Dough it was too late. The paramedic came down the mountain to give Julia the news.

Julia Nolten: He found him. And nothing could be done any more but he told me that he looked peaceful and he was lying on his back and he sat with him for a bit to just pay respect.

V/O The hardest for Julia was telling her children that their dad had been killed.

Julia Nolten: And that was of the most difficult things to tell them their father got killed. It was just...

V/O Two weeks earlier, a group of 9 hikers had been ambushed. Anwar Adams, an experienced hiker from Cape Town, and his group of friends entered the park from Baily’s Kloof side in Kalk Bay.

Anwar Adams: There is always someone that will put the hike on the tracking, what time we started, what hike we are doing, the amount of people in the hike and what time to expect us to complete the hike.

V/O Don and Yvonne Cormack, a British couple who belongs to the club, joined them that day. They have built close relationships with Adams and Pam Overmeyer.

Yvonne Cormack: Hiking attack victim: Pam got onto a big rock to take pictures of everybody else coming up the other side. And these other guys came over the rocks behind us. They got closer to us smiling and then they pulled the knives.

Claire: How many attackers were there?

Yvone: Only two

Yvonne Cormack: They came up towards Pam and he said “phones down” so Pam threw her phone at him. And then he said “bag” to Pam.

Claire Mawisa: Was the initial reaction to defend?

Don Cormack: Yah, I was trying to aim for his private parts and I got stabbed and that decapitated me if you like. But then I can’t remember much from there. I just layed on the ground with a pool of blood and I felt ill.

Yvonne Cormack: I could see all these knives going into Don, I could see him stab and it wasn’t just stabbing it was stab drag, and I just said “stop!” Don give him the bag!

V/O The attacker turned on Yvonne. Adams ran to a high point for signal. The second attacker ran after Adams.

Anwar Adams: I had my phone in my hand also trying to get tracking to alert them. There was no signal at that very point where we were in.

Claire Mawisa: What happened when you were just left with this one attacker?

Anwar Adams: I can’t remember any contact, I don’t remember anything. He must have actually had a good shot at my head.

V/O The attackers fled into the mountains with cell phones, rucksacks and cameras leaving a blood path in their wake.

Up audio: CMR call centre: “Cape Medical Response. Lindi speaking. What is your emergency?”

V/O A group of hikers that followed the blood trail put through an emergency call.

Up natural sound

V/O Andre Yon, from Cape Medical Rescue services was on duty that weekend.

Up natural sound

Andre Yon - Intermediate Life Support Paramedic: We received the call at about half past nine in the morning for multiple victims that hiked and was stabbed. When we arrived on the scene we discovered it was inaccessible for the ambulances due to the terrain.

V/O Yon attended to the critically injured till the helicopter arrived to hoist the patients.

Up natural sound

V/O AirMercy, Metro Rescue and various other support services performed the vital task of rescuing the injured hikers.

Up music

V/O Adams was in ICU for 3 days, Traut had severe injuries on his lower jaw and Cormack is still recovering from multiple stab wounds.

Newspaper clippings

V/O The week following the knife attack on the 9 victims, SANParks announced that they planned to beef up their security and roll out a Safety Plan. Andre van Schalkwyk from Table Mountain Watch has been part of negotiations on the Table Mountain Safety Forum. He says that they have been trying to get SANParks to look at a safety plan since September last year.

Andre van Schalkwyk: We started off trying to work with the park in 2007, 2008. It became an extremely difficult process. We eventually walked out and figured that we would do this on our own.

V/O Since the attacks in January this year van Schalkwyk has been actively working with the Table Mountain Security Action Group in finding solutions to fight crime in the Park.

Claire Mawisa: Whose responsibility is it to make sure the mountain users are safe in the park?

Andre van Schalkwyk: We look at SANParks as the first party in that process. In the second instance there is a responsibility on our part as well as hikers. There is SAPS and law enforcement and a number of other organisations they can help they can assist. SANParks needs to drive that. They need to own it.

Link: Sanparks says that visitor safety is a key component to their strategy with particular focus on the Table Mountain National Park. We invited SANParks to comment on the recent spate of attacks but after several attempts they refused to be interviewed on camera.

V/O Signboards like this one are seen at most entrances to the various areas of the park warning hikers of the dangers and recommending safety in numbers. Yet in a group of 9 hikers they did not stand a chance against only two attackers.

Link: the Table Mountain national Park spans 221 square km with 75% having open access points. The challenge is that there are reportedly only 52 rangers to patrol this vast area.

V/O Frank Dwyer is a registered mountain guide. He has been taking visitors onto the mountain for many years and has seen the impact that crime has had on the park.

Frank Dwyer: Mountain guide: The thing is it is affecting tourism in the long run.The original Hoerikwagga trail, that runs from Cape Point all the way through to Table Mountain that has been affected drastically because there are hotspot along the way.

Claire Mawisa: You are on the mountain more than the normal person, how often have you come across mountain rangers?

Frank Dwyer: We very, very seldom find the rangers on the mountain.

V/O It has been an emotional journey for the victims and their family.

Claire Mawisa: Has it changed the way you view going hiking now?

Don Cormack: My attitude to the mountain is I’ve got to go back. I have got to go back.

V/O And they did go back. In a solidarity walk to ‘claim back the mountain’

Up music

V/O Before Doug passed away he picked this bunch of flowers for Julia.

Julia Nolten: He picked them to give you the message that ‘don’t worry I am going but I am fine you know.”

V/O Doug’s death has added one more number to the growing list of victims. To date there had been 200 attacks in the Park over the last 6 years.

Hikers are being robbed and attacked at knife-point in Table Mountain National Park. In the last year 87 attacks took place, the latest victim was stabbed to death.

V/O Knife attacks on Table mountain visitors are out of control and no-one is completely safe anymore.
Yvonne Cormack: I could see all these knives going into Don, I could see him stab and it wasn’t just stabbing it was stab drag.

15 seconds
V/O Knife attacks in the Table Mountain National Park have gotten out of control. The latest victim was stabbed multiple times and bled to death.
Julia Nolten: And that was of the most difficult things to tell them their father got killed.

Yvonne Cormack: Hiking attack victim: Pam got onto a big rock to take pictures of everybody else coming up the other side. And these other guys came over the rocks behind us. They got closer to us smiling and then they pulled the knives. Claire: How many attackers were there? Yvone: Only two Yvonne Cormack: They came up towards Pam and he said “phones down” so Pam threw her phone at him. And then he said “bag” to Pam. Claire Mawisa: Was the initial reaction to defend? Don Cormack: Yah, I was trying to aim for his private parts and I got stabbed and that decapitated me if you like. But then I can’t remember much from there. I just layed on the ground with a pool of blood and I felt ill. Yvonne Cormack: I could see all these knives going into Don, I could see him stab and it wasn’t just stabbing it was stab drag, and I just said “stop!” Don give him the bag! V/O The attacker turned on Yvonne. Adams ran to a high point for signal. The second attacker ran after Adams. Anwar Adams: I had my phone in my hand also trying to get tracking to alert them. There was no signal at that very point where we were in. Claire Mawisa: What happened when you were just left with this one attacker? Anwar Adams: I can’t remember any contact, I don’t remember anything. He must have actually had a good shot at my head. V/O The attackers fled into the mountains with cell phones, rucksacks and cameras leaving a blood path in their wake. Up audio: CMR call centre: “Cape Medical Response. Lindi speaking. What is your emergency?” V/O A group of hikers that followed the blood trail put through an emergency call. Up natural sound V/O Andre Yon, from Cape Medical Rescue services was on duty that weekend. Up natural sound Andre Yon - Intermediate Life Support Paramedic: We received the call at about half past nine in the morning for multiple victims that hiked and was stabbed. When we arrived on the scene we discovered it was inaccessible for the ambulances due to the terrain. V/O Yon attended to the critically injured till the helicopter arrived to hoist the patients. Up natural sound V/O AirMercy, Metro Rescue and various other support services performed the vital task of rescuing the injured hikers. Up music V/O Adams was in ICU for 3 days, Traut had severe injuries on his lower jaw and Cormack is still recovering from multiple stab wounds. Newspaper clippings V/O The week following the knife attack on the 9 victims, SANParks announced that they planned to beef up their security and roll out a Safety Plan. Andre van Schalkwyk from Table Mountain Watch has been part of negotiations on the Table Mountain Safety Forum. He says that they have been trying to get SANParks to look at a safety plan since September last year. Andre van Schalkwyk: We started off trying to work with the park in 2007, 2008. It became an extremely difficult process. We eventually walked out and figured that we would do this on our own. V/O Since the attacks in January this year van Schalkwyk has been actively working with the Table Mountain Security Action Group in finding solutions to fight crime in the Park. Claire Mawisa: Whose responsibility is it to make sure the mountain users are safe in the park? Andre van Schalkwyk: We look at SANParks as the first party in that process. In the second instance there is a responsibility on our part as well as hikers. There is SAPS and law enforcement and a number of other organisations they can help they can assist. SANParks needs to drive that. They need to own it. Link: Sanparks says that visitor safety is a key component to their strategy with particular focus on the Table Mountain National Park. We invited SANParks to comment on the recent spate of attacks but after several attempts they refused to be interviewed on camera. V/O Signboards like this one are seen at most entrances to the various areas of the park warning hikers of the dangers and recommending safety in numbers. Yet in a group of 9 hikers they did not stand a chance against only two attackers. Link: the Table Mountain national Park spans 221 square km with 75% having open access points. The challenge is that there are reportedly only 52 rangers to patrol this vast area. V/O Frank Dwyer is a registered mountain guide. He has been taking visitors onto the mountain for many years and has seen the impact that crime has had on the park. Frank Dwyer: Mountain guide: The thing is it is affecting tourism in the long run.The original Hoerikwagga trail, that runs from Cape Point all the way through to Table Mountain that has been affected drastically because there are hotspot along the way. Claire Mawisa: You are on the mountain more than the normal person, how often have you come across mountain rangers? Frank Dwyer: We very, very seldom find the rangers on the mountain. V/O It has been an emotional journey for the victims and their family. Claire Mawisa: Has it changed the way you view going hiking now? Don Cormack: My attitude to the mountain is I’ve got to go back. I have got to go back. V/O And they did go back. In a solidarity walk to ‘claim back the mountain’ Up music V/O Before Doug passed away he picked this bunch of flowers for Julia. Julia Nolten: He picked them to give you the message that ‘don’t worry I am going but I am fine you know.” V/O Doug’s death has added one more number to the growing list of victims. To date there had been 200 attacks in the Park over the last 6 years. _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Promos: 10 seconds Hikers are being robbed and attacked at knife-point in Table Mountain National Park. In the last year 87 attacks took place, the latest victim was stabbed to death. 15 seconds V/O Knife attacks on Table mountain visitors are out of control and no-one is completely safe anymore. Yvonne Cormack: I could see all these knives going into Don, I could see him stab and it wasn’t just stabbing it was stab drag. 15 seconds V/O Knife attacks in the Table Mountain National Park have gotten out of control. The latest victim was stabbed multiple times and bled to death. Julia Nolten: And that was of the most difficult things to tell them their father got killed. _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Knife attacks in Table Mountain Reserve (5160) Annalise Lubbe 06 February 2018

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Horror attacks in the Table Mountain Reserve has spread fear amongst hikers. Tonight we bring you the story of a group of 9 hikers who were mugged at knifepoint in the Silvermine area.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We track the story of a horrific attack on 9 hikers in the Silvermine area of Table Mountain Reserve when a peaceful walk turns into a nightmare. This is just one of many recent attacks that have the community and visitors up in arms. Why is this happening and what is SANPark who are the custodians of the park doing about the drastic escalation of crime stats in the Reserve.
metadata.Summary: It was a Saturday morning when forty-nine-year Michael Traut from Retreat in Cape Town joined a small group of hikers on the Silvermine trail. The group was led by an experienced hiker Anwar Adams who gave a brief tooltalk before they set out on a comfortable pace. The group consisted of mostly elderly people, amongst them a British couple, Dan and Yvonne Cormack. It was a perfect sunny day with little wind and breathtaking scenes along the path to make this the perfect hike. Michael made small-talk with Dan and took a memorable picture on route. Little did he know that their fate was about to change. Two men appeared from behind a bush. They were flicking their knives and shouted at the group to hand over their phones, cameras and rucksacks. Dan put up a fight and got stabbed multiple times as he tried to resist. His wife Yvonne picked up a stick and hit the attacker shouting “leave my husband alone”. The attacker retaliated and stabbed Yvonne in the arm. Michael was next. A rock struck his jawbone and he was stabbed in the hand. Michael threw down his phone, camera and wallet then fell on the ground in a dizzy spell. Anwar ran to a high point for cellphone signal and to call for help. The second attacker ran after Anwar and and stopped him in his tracks with a blow on the head. Anwar fell down. The attackers fled from the scene with their loot.
metadata.Further information: On the same route that morning a group of young hikers saw blood spots on the rocks and started following the tracks. It led them to a secluded area high up in the mountain where they found Anwar and his group of hikers badly injured and in desperate need of medical attention. They put a call through to Cape Metro Rescue Services describing the situation and type of injuries. A helicopter, ambulance services and 4x4 rescue vehicles were dispatched. On the rescue operation was Andre Yon from Cape Medical Response (CMR) who were instrumental in the rescue mission and getting the patients to hospital. Anwar was in ICU for several days. His memory failed him to the exact events but his spirit is alive. When I visited him in hospital a few days ago he said: “More must be done. I want to get back so I can do something about this - be part of a solution.” Michael is back at his home in Retreat supported by his loving wife and daughter. He suffers from severe headaches, struggles to speak as he lost several teeth and injured his jawbone. “Bring back the death penalty, he says.” Yvonne told me that she will not allow this traumatic incident to keep her away from what she love most, and that is to walk in the mountains with her husband Don. He is still heavily traumatised by the event that changed their holiday into a nightmare. The attack on Anwar’s group was not an isolated incident. On that same morning 2 more knife attacks on hikers were reported in the Table Mountain Reserve. SANParks who were informed of the attacks said “Management would like to caution the public not to take the law in their own hands and not to interfere in any official law enforcement duties.” An ironic statement by Merle Collins, Regional Communications Manager of SANParks as their role is to monitor the Reserve and keep it safe. SANParks were nowhere to be seen on that day in the vicinity of the hikers, or on any other day, as many victims will repeat the same sentiment about their blatant absence in the Reserve on any given day. The horror scene described above is just one more on a list of growing statistics of armed attacks in the Table Mountain Reserve. Andre van Schalkwyk from a social network group, Table Mountain Watch have built up a database of stats that show pre-2000 crime in the Park was remarkably low; it peaked in 2004; increased in 2008 and rose dramatically in 2011 and beyond. Van Schalkwyk has tried to set up a Safety Forum network to meet monthly with the Park, City Metro Police, Law Enforcement, SAPS, Table Mountain Park Safety rangers and even Metro Traffic to access sensitive areas or hot spots where crime is prevalent. But this has amounted to nought as SANParks claim “we will look after our own safety’. But crime speaks volumes. SANParks is clearly not capable of performing their task successfully and for this reason private security companies have been contracted to protect communities. All along the south Peninsula neighbourhood watch have been instituted to fight crime. However security guards have been told in no uncertain terms to “get off SANParks ground” when they try and protect citizens. Joseph Padbury of Komwatch (Kommetjie Neighbourhood Watch) recalls an incident where two people were attacked on Noordhoek beach hours after SANParks patrol unit told them to get off the beach. (Noordhoek Beach and Sandy Bay are the only two beaches in Cape Town that falls under SANParks protection and is therefor their responsibility to keep these areas safe.) According to SANParks they have 52 dedicated trained staff equipped with dogs, vehicles and radios to monitor and patrol the 221 sq km Park. They take the view that “it is a vast open area” but do not welcome any assistance from the outside. Frank Dwyer, a registered mountain tour-guide for 30 years here in the Cape has seen the numbers drop as crime escalates. Some overnight hiking camps have been abandoned and closed for ‘safety reasons’. He is saddened by the lack of concern from the Parks to keep this national heritage site a ‘must see attraction’ for both local and international tourists. We add to our story the latest stabbing on a hiker two weeks after the stabbing on the 9 hiker took place. Julia and Douglas Nolten were hiking in the same are when Douglas was stabbed multiple times and eventually bled to death. Our story: We will hear from the victims who were held at knifepoint and share their horrific story of what they experienced on that Saturday morning hike. We will put SANParks on the spot on why they have not been visible enough to protect hikers from incidents like these and there lack of cooperation with other organisations to ‘work together’ in fighting crime. Through this programme I hope to bring a sense of urgency to taking action by all the relevant parties in bringing down the crime statistics and making the Table Mountain Reserve a safe place for everyone to enjoy again.
